The hero follows Linear's stack — slogan and lede on the left, then the desktop app at the container's full width, its sidebar, chief header, thread and composer drawn after the app's own chrome; the hero's tagline and CTA pair leave, with the nav and CTA footer carrying the actions. The OG share card drops its copy for a lone centered wordmark, so one image serves every locale.
- **Plans — the project cap is per plan**: The project cap used to be one number for every plan (6), treating a paid team like a free one. It now lives in each plan's limits — Pro teams get 20 projects, Free teams 6 — and the sidebar, the new-project error, the pricing page and the upgrade table all read the plan's number. A refused create now also tracks a quota hit and carries a sentence the chief can relay; existing projects survive a downgrade, only creating past the cap is refused.
- **App — the sidebar's project and resource sections fold**: The sidebar used to run every project and resource straight down the rail. Both section headers now toggle their section — the chevron rides the far-edge column a row gives its pin, so the labels keep the left edge they share with their rows, and a folded section holding the screen you're on takes the active tint. The docked rail folds with them, one chevron per group standing in for the header it has no room for; the rules above Schedules and between the rail's groups are gone, and both folds are stored per device. The landing page's hero mock follows the same sidebar.
- **App — the plan chip moves onto the team glyph**: The FREE/PRO/TRIAL chip beside the team name is gone; the plan now reads off the glyph's tint — amber for a paid team, indigo while a trial's clock runs, and the plain bordered box every other nav row wears for free. The name gets the whole row back, and the collapsed rail's team icon carries the same colour, so both states say the same thing.
- **App — a deployed tab keeps loading, and learns it is stale**: A tab opened before a deploy carried only its own build's chunks, so every lazy import afterwards — avatars, syntax highlighting, onboarding — failed until a manual reload. CI now archives each build's static assets and the pod backfills whatever chunk it lacks from there; on the client a failed lazy import retries instead of caching the failure, and a fatal load error reloads the page once. API responses carry a build header, so a tab that notices a newer build offers a reload.
- **Feedback — staff can see a ticket's images in the app**: Every attachment in the app resolves through one preview endpoint, which admitted team members only — so a staff member reading someone else's ticket got a 403 and a skeleton that never resolved. Staff now pass that gate (the same read the impersonation lens already grants), and an image whose URL can't be fetched falls back to the document row instead of a blank tile.

## 2026-09-02

- **Models — Claude Fable 5.1 lands on five providers**: The catalog gains Claude Fable 5.1 across Anthropic, Bedrock (base/global/us — no eu variant upstream yet), OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway and Cloudflare AI Gateway, all at 10/50 with a 0.25 cache-read price and a 1M context window, image input and reasoning levels (xhigh/max); OpenRouter's fable-latest alias follows to 0.25 cache-read. Copilot and OpenCode Zen don't serve 5.1 yet. The entries are hand-written — pi-ai 0.84.4 doesn't ship the model.
- **Landing — a localized static site ships**: The public site now prerenders localized static pages — English stays unprefixed, while Simplified Chinese /zh, Traditional /zh-TW and Japanese /ja each carry their code as the first segment, and old addresses like /pricing rewrite to /en/pricing, redirecting to the reader's remembered locale. Every page gains canonical, hreflang and OG tags, and the site adds JSON-LD structured data (organization, website, software application with offers, FAQ, breadcrumbs and articles), a sitemap with alternates, and /llms.txt plus /llms-full.txt; login, upgrade and handshake pages are tightened to noindex in robots. An untranslated doc still renders under localized chrome but canonicals to English and stays out of hreflang and the sitemap. The legal pages move through the docs renderer (real anchors), /compare and /use-cases are collected as Markdown with their first entries shipping as drafts; along the way the /docs index title key, the pricing h1 and the docs <main> are fixed, and old dashboard redirects become 308s.
- **File preview — LaTeX prose folds into paragraphs**: TeX reads a lone newline as a space, but the projection handed every source newline to the Markdown renderer, which painted it as a line break — so an 80-column paper rendered one source line per screen line. Prose now folds onto its paragraph (or the list item it continues); blank lines, `\\`, `\par` and page breaks still break. Headings, list items, table rows, images and own-line blocks keep their lines, and environment boundaries outside lists gain a blank so following text can't fold into the last item or line. IEEEkeywords now renders as an Index Terms label.
- **File preview — algorithmic pseudocode renders as a list**: The algorithmic environment used to land inside a latex fence, which locked its math away from the math renderer — and pseudocode is mostly math. algorithmic bodies now become one list item per statement (keywords bold, comments marked the way algorithmicx draws them), after math protection so a multi-line formula is already one token and its continuation lines fold into the statement. verbatim and lstlisting keep their fence.
- **Diffs — image previews load instantly and gain an eye button**: Expanding an image card used to be slow every time — hosts pass the conv branch as gitRef, whose raw responses are no-store, and every mount minted its own preview token first. The diff response now carries the change set's immutable headSha, the changes view reads raw content at it (sha responses cache forever), and token mints are shared per (project, ref) so concurrent mounts and re-expands stop paying the round trip. Image rows also had no preview button (previewKind covers text-content kinds only) — DiffPreview now grows an image kind plus the commit to read from, dispatched to ImageFilePreview; removed files read the merge-base side, as the inline preview already did.
- **Sessions — long-session backups no longer silently go stale**: pi's compaction appends a summary but never shrinks the file, so a long chief session kept every summarized turn on disk (76MB holding 1.2MB of live context) and re-uploaded all of it every turn until the upload could no longer finish in time — one chief's backup has been silently stale since 08-27. Opening a session now cuts everything before the second-latest compaction's kept window, carrying the latest model and thinking-level entries forward so the SDK reads the same context and settings; rewinding older than that window takes the existing reset-to-empty path.
- **Memory — the tidy nudge goes quiet on a plateau**: The sweep woke every pressured chief once a day regardless of what the last wake changed, so a chief that reviewed its memory and kept it all was woken again tomorrow — seven days, six wakes, pressure never moving. A nudge now records the percentage it fired at (a 30-day Redis mark); the next one waits for pressure to climb 20 points past that mark or for the mark to age out, with the 24-hour lock kept as the floor. The note also names how many entries now reach the chief title-only each turn — the real cost of growth — and says plainly that keeping what is worth keeping ends the reminders.

## 2026-09-01

- **Team page — agents render as a card grid**: The team page's default view switches from a list to a card grid, one card per agent — a large avatar with name, model and role lines, then a skills chip row (up to three chips, a +N for the rest, and a dashed placeholder when none are set). Whenever any member has skills the row stays on for every card, keeping the grid even. Human members show name and email only in the team-settings roster. The org chart drops its user column, so the chief leads straight into the agent stack; the members payload now carries agent descriptions and skill ids, and the agent detail page's model-unconfigured notice gets breathing room from its dividers.
- **File preview — LaTeX papers render in place**: The file preview adds .tex support, projecting a paper into Markdown for the existing Markdown/math pipeline — sections, lists, tables, figures and citations all come through, with every math region passed verbatim. Reviewing a LaTeX paper in-app used to mean a hand-built tex→md conversion for every revision.
- **Chief — the todos entry survives an all-done board**: The header progress ring was the only path to the chief's todos board, and it unmounted at zero open todos, stranding the settled history. It now rests as a check badge at zero, the hover card gains an all-done row that still links to the board, and the board seeds its phase filter with done/closed when nothing is open so it no longer lands on an empty Open bucket.
- **Chat — your turns ride their own bubble**: In the app and the landing demo alike, the user's own words now sit in a content-hugging bubble (left-aligned, avatar kept) so the asker reads apart from the chief at a glance. Steer bodies keep their margin-note bar, and the clamp fade now paints the ground it actually covers.
- **Chat — a web-page answer reads as a clearer error**: When a custom provider's relay domain dies, the answer to the chief can be a 403 plus a full HTML page (a panel block page, a WAF challenge, a gateway login) — and that markup used to land verbatim in the chat bubble. It's now recognized as "the model service answered with a web page, not an API response": the bubble shows a translated headline and hint, with the raw page folded behind the disclosure. Pages with a clear status still keep their sharper remedies — a 404 reads as a bad Base URL, a 502 as an upstream failure.
- **Chat — the compaction notice keeps just the point**: The context-compaction notice drops its explainer clause, so "🧹 Compacted context — older turns summarized, recent kept" becomes "🧹 Compacted context" (and the auto variant likewise); the breakdown read as noise in every locale.
- **Landing — the hero leads with effortless Agent teams and one-sentence dispatch**: The hero title changes from "Less effort, ship faster" to "Effortless Agent teams", and the subtitle from "Todos is a minimal agent workspace. Command a whole team through a single agent…" to "Todos puts an Agent team to work in one sentence — models and roles auto-assigned, working in parallel, delivering efficiently." All four locales updated.
- **Landing — the coding-agent FAQ contrasts, the overview follows suit**: The answer to "How does Todos differ from Claude, Codex and other coding agents?" drops the complementarity claim for a direct contrast — coding agents are session-centric (one agent per session, unsearchable history, attention spent babysitting), while Todos is task-centric (a chief-run team of agents with roles and memory, searchable past tasks, goals and key decisions only). The docs overview opening now leads with the same frame — minimal agent workspace, task-centric — with the fit examples kept in a second paragraph. All four locales updated.
- **Landing — the hero chat replays a blog's full launch**: The homepage demo now runs a blog from idea to inkwell.blog going live — the ask fans out into three parallel todos (pages, Markdown rendering, deploy pipeline), the architect's independent review catches a missing HTML escape before the first version merges, the user's change requests route to the right engineers, and their go-ahead ships the site, both addresses in accent ink.

## 2026-08-31

- **MCP — the built-in server opens to every coding agent**: Todos ships a built-in MCP server, and it now has a public home at /mcp — a three-step guide (one remote URL and one Bearer API key, no OAuth, nothing to install) plus a rundown of what a connected agent can do, from reading the board to dispatching builds and requesting review. The header nav gains an MCP entry, the home showcase adds a "One list for every agent" selling point (Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sharing one board), and the /features MCP card moves up to fourth. The read-only surface widens too: skills, machines, and the GitHub readers — issues, pull requests and CI workflow runs — now reach MCP callers, so an agent can turn an issue straight into a todo and check PR or CI state (GitHub-backed projects only).
- **MCP — a build started over MCP notifies you and says so**: A build dispatched by an MCP-connected agent used to inherit the chief's "it reports back" behavior, so the owner was never notified, and the transcript gave no hint of where the turn came from. MCP-started builds now notify the owner like any web-started build, and the transcript's provenance line reads "Started over MCP".
- **Landing — the positioning settles on a minimal agent workspace**: The hero subtitle now opens by naming Todos a minimal agent workspace instead of an efficient agent task engine, and the page title, meta description and OG image slogan all carry the same workspace positioning. The Pro card's price note also stops restating the trial terms and instead names what the plan ships — hosted sandboxes and built-in models, out of the box.

## 2026-08-30

- **Chat — a silent machine now says so**: A machine that went quiet mid-turn used to leave the thread stuck on its last stage frame ("Preparing…") for the whole ten-minute offline grace, reading as a stall. The thread now shows "Machine unreachable" the moment the sweep notices, and clears it when the machine recovers — so a dead machine is named instead of left to look frozen. The status label also says "Retrying 2/3" instead of "Working 2/3", since it now only describes the turn itself.
- **Builds — a stalled output recovers in 30 seconds**: The stream idle watchdog used one 120-second bound for every mid-stream silence, so a turn whose model stopped emitting output hung for two full minutes before the retry. Output silence now cuts at 30 seconds while thinking keeps its 120, so a dead connection is caught — and the turn retried — much sooner.
- **Models — the catalog is served from one static file**: Built-in providers' model definitions now come from a single static catalog (modelCatalog.json — 38 providers, 1,279 models) instead of pi's built-in table, so a pi upgrade no longer silently changes which models exist. GPT-5.6's context window is corrected to OpenAI's published figures (openai 1,050,000 tokens; openai-codex 872,000; luna stays 272,000), and openai-codex now ships as a custom provider so the catalog decides its models on any released CLI.
- **Features — three cards join the grid**: /features gains "Chief supervision" (the Chief carries each todo through dispatch, review, confirm and merge on its own), "Runs across machines" (machines form one cluster; each task goes to whichever is idle, or is pinned to the one you name), and "Third-party MCP servers" (register external MCP servers for the team and grant them to agents alongside the built-in tools), in all four languages.
- **Landing — the FAQ answers are rewritten and tracked**: The landing answers now lead with what Todos is for — an agent task engine for long, low-interaction, multi-agent work — and place it beside coding agents (Claude, Codex) rather than cloud agents; pricing leads with what a team is and why it exists; mobile drops the PWA wording for the path people actually take; models cite the 700+ figure; subscriptions add XAI; execution mentions the Pro sandbox. A new pricing FAQ explains what a team is.

## 2026-08-29

- **Features page — narrowed to the core**: /features is now titled "Core features" with no lede, and the cards are rewritten around the agent-task-engine positioning — "Standing chief" becomes "Agent chief" wearing the sidebar's chief glyph, "Live preview" joins, BYOK becomes "BYOC & BYOK" and moves up, and six cards go (structured questions, steer mid-run, conversation rewind, screenshot markup, four mentions, notifications on your terms); most remaining descriptions are shorter, in all four languages.
- **Landing — the Stories page retires**: Three first-person customer accounts no longer fit what Todos is — an agent task engine — so /use-cases is gone, along with its nav, footer and home-page entries; the old address redirects permanently to the home page, and the app's team setup no longer quotes the three stories.
- **Landing — "an efficient agent task engine" becomes the through-line**: The hero subtitle and the docs overview now open by naming Todos an efficient agent task engine, and FAQ 9's "what kinds of work" answer names the engine and lists concrete examples — a software product PoC, algorithm experiments, batch server patrols, migrating a codebase, large-scale data processing, LLM evaluations, weekly and daily reports — closing on cross-machine and scheduled runs.
- **Landing — the hero's second button returns**: The outline CTA beside "start free" is back as a link to the features page, labelled "Core features", which also renames the link under the selling points.
- **Models — backport Tencent Hy4 on OpenRouter**: tencent/hy4-preview joined OpenRouter's public catalog after pi 0.84.3's snapshot, so it is backported — 1M context window, reasoning levels off/low/high — and a team on its own OpenRouter key can now select it.
- **Email — the welcome mail introduces the product, not the founder**: The welcome mail was a personal letter from the founder; it now reads as product copy — three selling points, then a nudge to open the workspace, with docs and support links — sent from the same no-reply address as every other mail. The four translations now actually send: signup reads the locale instead of always sending English.
- **App — HTML files render in isolated previews on mobile**: Mobile now renders HTML files in isolated previews with the same sandbox policy as web, instead of a dead end.

## 2026-08-28

- **Chief — the chief can now grant team secrets**: Secrets were the one agent grant kept off the chief's tools. create_agent and update_agent now take secret ids (or ["*"]) the way they already took skills and MCP servers, the admin routes and the chief share one grant schema, and every grant list is deduped — so a repeated id no longer renders twice, and the docs that said secrets stay human-only are updated.
- **App — the sidebar folds its project list and supports pinning**: The drawer listed every project of the team; it now shows the first five with a "Show all (N)" row (remembered per device), and projects can be pinned from the project page header — pinned rows sit first, newest pin on top, tap to unpin. Pins live on the account, so every device agrees.
- **App — the roster names the machines it warns about**: Offline and outdated machine banners now name the machines, each name a link to that machine's page, and one "have the chief upgrade it" button covers every listed machine. The home screen floats a notice when the chief has nowhere to run — its pinned machine is offline, or, unpinned, no machine is up at all.
- **App — the context meter shows only when it matters**: The context-window pie in the header now appears only from 85% (the red threshold); the full read-out moves into chief settings, shared with the "release window" action. The agent tab regroups — the machine row joins the agent card, and context usage sits with the compaction model.
- **App — what's-new dots drop, majors open once**: The unread dot on the sidebar avatar and beside "What's new" is gone; a major entry opens the panel on its own, a minor one waits on the panel's updates tab. Pinned projects is promoted to major so it opens once for everyone.
- **Projects — the per-team project cap is enforced atomically**: Ten concurrent "create project" calls could all read the same count and pass, landing ten projects on a team capped at six. The slot is now taken in one scripted update, so at most the cap can ever pass.

## 2026-08-27

- **Models — GLM-5.3-Flash ships, the Ox Alpha stealth ids retire**: Zhipu released glm-5.3-flash on Aug 26, and it turns out to be what OpenRouter and Zen had been serving as "Ox Alpha" — stealth/ox-alpha is now gone from OpenRouter entirely, and Zen's ox-alpha-free is marked deprecated. The real ids land on four endpoints — Z.AI Coding Plan's global and China lines, Zen Go, and OpenRouter — and the three stealth patches are dropped. It's GLM's first natively multimodal model, taking images, which is the only reason to reach for Flash over GLM-5.3 on a plan that carries both. Pricing: the Coding Plan endpoints stay at 0 (a subscription pays, not a token count); Zen Go and OpenRouter bill at the launch promotion (0.075 input / 0.25 output / 0.015 cache read, halved through 2026-09-09). The thinking picker now lists only the three published efforts — low/high/max — instead of six entries where four were the same request under another name.
- **Machines — have the chief run a machine's CLI upgrade**: The machine page's update banner used to just hand you two commands to paste yourself. It now leads with a "have the chief upgrade it" button: clicking sends a self-contained prompt and hands over to the conversation, where the chief creates a todo, pins the build to that machine, and has the agent run `npm install -g @todos-dev/cli@latest` in place, with `tds restart` as the last step (the restart cuts the build off — expected, the detached helper finishes the upgrade in the background), then re-reads machines to confirm the version and reports back. The steps ride the sent message rather than the chief's system prompt, so this rarely-used flow costs nothing on every other turn. The button is admin-only (the chief acts as you); the manual commands fold behind a disclosure, staying expanded for non-admins whose only path they are.
- **Chat — the turn status shows one stage at a time, and a spinner replaces "working"**: The stage line used to concatenate every stage the turn had passed ("connecting to machine... preparing... connecting to model...") and kept them on screen, since stages only ever upgrade and never clear — stale text left hovering above a turn the model was already writing. It now renders only the stage currently running, alone, and disappears once the model finishes (or on the first thinking block, for an older CLI). The "working…" word and its animating ellipsis are replaced by a terminal-style braille spinner — one loader on the row instead of two. The spinner is drawn as views rather than set as text, because braille ink sits at a different height in each platform's fallback font (small and high on iOS, low on web); only drawing can hold it centred against the elapsed count so the digits never shift.
- **Chat — unparsed tool calls no longer wear a clean "done"**: A custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool-call parsing disabled returns the model's raw template — tool calls arrive as text tags, never actually run, and the turn ends looking finished. The settled body is now checked for those leaked tags (`<tool_call>`, `<function=`, `[TOOL_CALLS]`) and the status line turns to an amber notice telling you to enable tool parsing on the endpoint. It's render-time only, nothing persisted, so existing broken turns warn too.
- **Chief — empty-state cards now fill the composer instead of sending**: Tapping an empty-state example card used to send it straight out, with no room to edit. It now prefills the composer and focuses it, so you can adjust before sending. The hint is also trimmed to a single line and names the exit: "Pick a simple example to start with — you can delete it when you're done," so a first-time reader isn't left weighing whether picking one commits to something.
- **Landing — the subtitle now names the orchestration itself**: The subtitle used to define the product as a workspace and promise team-scale output without ever saying what it does. It now names the shape: "Todos lets one agent run a team of agents — assigning each its own model and role, so they get the job done together, fast." All four locales updated.

## 2026-08-26

- **Builds — a stuck command can now be interrupted mid-run**: When a build agent was wedged on a command (a recursive grep can run for ten-plus minutes), all you could do was send a steer, which the agent wouldn't see until the command's own timeout finally fired — the steer was a dead letter. The expanded trace's running tool row now carries a stop button: click it, optionally add a reason (a concise default is sent if you leave it blank), and the command is killed in place so the agent reads your message at the next tool boundary and continues another way. A real cancel still looks like a cancel rather than an interrupt, and with nothing running the button degrades to a plain steer; on machines with a tds CLI older than 0.1.49 the interrupt arrives as an ordinary message. The expanded trace also gains a bottom collapse, so a long trace folds without scrolling back to its trailer.
- **Builds — context compaction no longer overflows and resets the conversation**: pi's stock in-loop compaction only tripped at the window's very edge (98.4% of a 1M window), where the summarization request itself overflowed the summary model and the conversation could only be reset. The server now delivers the trigger at claim time — by default 80% of the window — and trims old tool results first (2k characters of head kept, images dropped), so the summary request no longer tracks occupancy. Compaction is finally visible: the in-flight bubble lights a "compacting" label, a "compacted" notice lands after the turn, and each compaction reports its token counts.
- **Chief — pick a faster model for context compaction**: The in-loop compaction summary always ran on the conversation's own model — an opus-class chief paid opus-class latency for a mechanical summary, and the summary call's cost was invisible. Chief settings now have a compaction model: pick any model from the team catalog to do the summarizing (absent, it falls back to the chief's own model), so a faster, cheaper model takes the mechanical work. The trim dials (tool-result chars, text chars, summary token cap) ride every step from the server, and every failure degrades — ending back on pi's stock compaction path.
- **Chat — web threads page through history, and Safari stops checkerboarding**: The message list fetched a fixed newest-200 window in one go, and on long threads Safari checkerboarded under the per-row layout and paint. Messages now arrive as 50-message pages over a cursor, and reaching the top loads the next older page; rows outside the newest 24 render under content-visibility so the browser skips off-screen layout and paint. Code fences also mount their horizontal scroller only when a line actually overflows, instead of paying a compositing layer per fence.
- **Chat — the web thread re-pins when the scroller itself resizes**: The stick-to-bottom library's ResizeObserver watched only the content element, so when the scroller itself shrank — the composer growing as iOS's late safe-area inset lands on a PWA cold boot, or the web keyboard opening — a pinned thread's bottom slid under the composer until the next explicit re-pin a network round trip later. The scroller is now observed too and the pin is held synchronously before paint, so the displacement never shows; a reader scrolled up in history is left alone.
- **CLI v0.1.49**: auto context compaction (with a configurable compaction model) and mid-task interruption of stuck commands ship in this release — machines must upgrade to 0.1.49 to get them; branch pushes are also more reliable, and openai-codex moves to SSE so long reasoning no longer drops on proxied connections.

## 2026-08-25

- **Chief — a leaner prompt, a docs tool, and sharper approval calls**: The chief's standing prompt carried 7.7k characters of inlined product facts — its largest section, drifting freely from the published docs it duplicated — and its approval rule had no way to honor a standing "you decide, don't ask me". The prompt is now about 15% smaller: the product section keeps only behavior rules and names its hot docs, and a new chief-only `docs` tool returns the published guide verbatim on demand, so product answers track the latest docs instead of memory. The approval rule gains standing delegation — a durable "you decide / don't ask me" is saved to memory and carries the agreed route forward without per-step confirmation, with hard exclusions (cards, new credentials, publishing, team reshaping, real forks). Dispatching now owns the route: every completion report ends with the next step — started, or one concrete recommendation the user can approve with a word — and communication leads with the outcome, one screen, in the user's language at their level. The fresh-team bootstrap also injects only while the roster has no agent beyond the chief, so an established team stops carrying it.
- **Memory — the chief now tidies its own memory**: A chief whose memory crept past 80% of either cap (entry count or inject budget) had to remember to prune on its own — the only nudge was a line in save_memory's return, invisible once it stopped touching the memory tools. An hourly sweep now finds pressured chiefs and arms an immediately-due wake carrying the tidy-up instruction; the chief consolidates related entries, deletes stale ones, and adds expiries to short-lived state. A 24-hour cooldown per agent keeps it from nagging, and it reports back only if the cleanup surfaces something you should know.
- **Chief — todo specs written more faithfully**: A week of chief sessions showed four recurring spec failures: inferred details passed off as user-confirmed, vague degree asks ("brighter") hardened into invented acceptance numbers, one-line requests expanded into pre-built implementation pipelines before any clarification, and third-party figures entering deliverables without source or basis. create_todo's guidance now states each rule — "confirmed" means the user said it, other details carry their source; degree numbers are marked starting values, never acceptance criteria; an open-shaped ask gets the clarify/design slice alone; third-party figures carry source and basis, with conclusions left to the build. Wake updates now close like any completion report — with the next step.
- **Chief — an identical create no longer mints duplicate todos**: A retry storm re-issuing one create_todo could mint ten copies of the same todo over nine minutes. An identical create — same project, title and spec — within ten minutes now returns the existing todo instead of a duplicate, checked before the daily cap so a storm at the cap boundary still resolves to its todo.
- **Providers — model discovery works when editing a stored provider**: The edit form's key field is write-only and blank, so every discovery from the edit dialog probed a keyed endpoint with no credential and failed as "couldn't connect". The discover route now probes with the row's stored credential (the key never leaves the server), and a 401/403 reads as "key rejected" rather than blaming the connection.
- **Builds — a transport failure names its hop instead of blaming the platform**: When a model call timed out or a provider was unreachable, the transcript's bare "fetch failed" / "Request timed out" left readers to invent a cause — and the chief once read it as server instability and told the user so, when the fault was the machine's own just-repaired proxy. The transcript now appends the origin for model_timeout / provider_unreachable on non-managed providers: the call was dialed directly from the build machine, so that machine's own network or proxy is on the path — the platform is not.
- **Builds — steering at a wedged command no longer blanks the stuck tool**: The moment a user steered at a wedged command, the panel went blank about which tool was stuck — exactly when that name mattered most — because the steer pair advanced the build's sequence counter and the "counter unmoved = still inside the tool" check failed. The steer frames are now published without touching the counter, so the stuck tool stays named.
- **App — a broken keychain no longer reads as a sign-in loop**: A corrupted keychain entry (backup restore, OS upgrade) used to present as an unexplained sign-in loop: a failed read latched into a process-wide logout, and a failed write threw the whole sign-in away. The memory copy is now the source of truth — a failed read retries on the next foreground, a failed write self-heals by deleting the wreck and retrying once, and each failure files a report. The entry also moves to AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK so locked-screen background launches can read it.
- **App — a cold boot no longer shows a finished turn as 处理中**: A cached in-flight turn carried its body but also its "running" state, which the client can't keep current while a PWA is backgrounded or killed. On a cold boot that stale state seeded the last turn as 处理中 until the boot fetch landed. The cache now seeds the row's body alone, leaving the turn's live state to the boot fetch / SSE reconnect — the only sources that know whether it actually finished.
- **App — the web composer types without a per-keystroke reflow**: react-native-web read scrollHeight inside every input event — a forced whole-page reflow per keystroke, worst on long threads. Browsers with field-sizing: content now grow the textarea natively, so the JS measuring drops out of typing entirely, and the edit handler reuses the chip document it already built instead of folding the wire text twice per keystroke.
- **Skills — memory and skill edits leave an audit trail**: Agent memories and skills now live in a per-team git repo, so every change is a commit — git log/diff is the modification history these stores never had. Commits carry the acting actor as author, an optional reason, and conversation refs; admin memory edits and skill deletes accept a reason, and a skill delete carries its reason through the confirm card into the deletion commit.

## 2026-08-24

- **Landing — the selling points retold as chief conversations**: The home page's six selling points now speak one visual language: the chief conversation. The first point becomes the thesis — team building, dispatch, review, schedules and reports all happen in that one conversation — proved by three swappable scenes (assemble, dispatch, catch-up). Parallel delivery, independent review and self-improving memory each replay as a progressive chat, the last reusing the real memory-system notice; a new overnight section shows the chief running the night shift on a standing authorization, sitting right after parallel delivery. A note under the demos states the scope: any computer-based work that splits into assignable tasks with verifiable output. Mobile step captions become tappable labelled chips instead of dot indicators.
- **What's new — a capabilities tab carries the home page's demos**: The What's new dialog only answered "what changed lately" — what the product does at all was told once, on the marketing home page, to people who hadn't signed up yet, and a signed-in reader had no way back to it. The dialog now has two tabs in its header: unread announcements lead when there are any, otherwise the capability side does. Only a visit to the announcements tab advances the read cursor, so browsing capabilities can't swallow an unread notice. The capability side replays the home page's six selling points exactly as they appear there — drawn once by the server at /embed/capabilities, framed on web and shown in a WebView on native, with a prose-card fallback when the page can't be reached. The home page copy also tightened: "Agents deliver in parallel" → "Faster delivery in parallel", "Self-improving agents" → "Memory that maintains itself", and the setup body now ends on "No setup needed — it works out of the box".
- **Providers — probe and verify custom endpoints from your device**: Discovery and save-time verification ran only from the server's egress, so a locally hosted endpoint — Ollama on localhost, a LAN gateway — could never be probed, even though builds reach it fine from the executor machine. The probe now runs from your device first, falling back to the server when the browser's CORS rules block it; when a server-side verify fails as unreachable, the client re-verifies with one minimal request and saves, telling you it verified from this device. The failure copy splits: connection failures ask you to check the address, and only a listening-but-blocked endpoint gets the CORS guidance (OLLAMA_ORIGINS, LM Studio's Enable CORS, the browser's local-network prompt).
- **Providers — custom models can declare image input**: A custom provider model had no way to carry image input — the editor never held it, so every custom model fell to the text-only default and images were stripped client-side before the request, however multimodal the real model is. The model editor now has an images toggle next to reasoning, and discovery pre-checks it from OpenRouter's input modalities.
- **Providers — edit custom models in a nested dialog**: The custom-provider form rendered two model UIs inline — discovered rows as checkbox toggles, manual rows as three stacked inputs — which ballooned the dialog once discovery returned a long list. Both are now one list: each row shows the id, label and a capability summary, ✕ removes it, and tapping opens a single model form (id, label, context window, images, reasoning and its cap) used for adding and editing alike. Discovery now merges new ids into the list instead of replacing it.
- **Models — openai-codex no longer dies mid-thought on some proxies**: pi's WebSocket-first transport carries no bytes while codex reasons, so proxies on the machine's path killed the connection minutes into a long thinking stretch and streamed thinking arrived only at the end. The official codex CLI ships SSE, where summary deltas keep the stream alive. Transport is now server policy: openai-codex runs over SSE — a machine's own pi settings still outrank it, and with nothing delivered pi's default stands untouched.
- **Files — a markdown preview's links navigate inside the app**: A README's `./page2.md` was a real link that the browser resolved against the app's own URL, leaving for a 404 wearing the product's domain. The markdown preview now resolves relative and root-relative links against the file they were written in, opens them on the Files page — feeding the same back/forward trail the HTML preview feeds — scrolls `#section` links to the right heading, and loads relative images off the signed raw route. Chat bodies pass no file context, so their links and images keep their behaviour.
- **Builds — the merge click answers immediately**: Merge & Done used to hold its HTTP response — and the confirm dialog's spinner — through opening a PR and polling mergeability, up to ~6.5s of fixed backoff. The route now runs only the network-free precheck, claims the todo as building (closing the double-click window), and answers at once; the GitHub work continues in the background and settles the claim, rolling back to review when blocked. A blocked state found after the fact — and a failed merge turn, which never notified at all — now lands as a merge_blocked notification whose snippet carries the concrete reason.
- **Chat — OpenAI citation markers no longer show as tofu**: gpt models cite web-search results as private-use-area spans referencing sources we never receive; with no cleanup they reached the reader as tofu boxes around raw `turn0search0` text. The markdown normalizer now drops complete spans, an unterminated one still streaming in, and any stray delimiter — one pass covers both renderers and repairs already-persisted messages at render time.
- **Chat — the web thread no longer shudders on a cold boot**: Stock use-stick-to-bottom waited for a frame before every resize correction, so the web thread painted 1-2 displaced frames on each height change — a cold boot lands several in a row, each a visible jolt on a busy main thread. The library is patched to pin resizes synchronously before paint, chips persist with the message cache so a cache-seeded first frame paints real cards instead of skeletons, and measured image aspect ratios are cached so a reopened thread paints images at their real height immediately.
- **App — error toasts and banners read as text, not raw JS**: Errors surfaced as toasts or banners used to show raw exception text in places — a network failure read as whatever the fetch layer threw. Every failure path now runs through one localizer: network errors map to a "check your connection" line, known server codes keep their specific messages, and anything unmapped falls back to a generic failure line with the raw error kept in the console. Web also gains the same 15s request timeout native has, so a dead connection errors instead of hanging.
- **App — a flaky network no longer bounces a configured team to onboarding**: The setup gate wrote empty machine/model rows whenever its snapshot fetch failed, which read a flaky network as an unconfigured team and replaced the current screen with onboarding. Only a successful response's empty rows may say that now: on failure the gate stays "not ready" and retries after 5s, the same cadence the onboarding poll already uses.
- **App — the standalone PWA opens from cache instead of a spinner**: A standalone PWA reloads the whole document on every back-swipe or foreground return, and three first-paint resources still waited on the network each time: the onboarding gate, the member roster, and the notification inbox. All three now follow the stale-while-revalidate pattern the rest of the app uses, so a cold start paints the last-known state immediately and refreshes behind it.

## 2026-08-23

- **Landing — the hero leads with "Less effort, Ship faster"**: The home page's headline moves from "Think deeper, Ship faster" to a direct promise of effort saved — "Less effort, Ship faster" — and the subtitle now says you hand execution off to agents and deliver what used to take a whole team. The tagline under it changed too: out goes the no-credit-card line and the model-name roll call, in come the three things that actually differentiate — BYOC and BYOK, 700+ models, and built on Pi. All four locales updated.
- **Landing — selling points trimmed and renamed**: The selling points below the fold drop from six sections to five. "Cost" leaves the home page (spend is still itemized on /features' usage card), and "live preview" moves to the end so the deliverables read as the payoff rather than a step in the middle of the run. The two remaining headings now say what the section shows rather than what Todos cares about — "Independent agent review" and "Self-improving agents" — and the latter's body credits the half that was missing, that agents draw their own lessons from a round into memory, not just the skills you hand them.
- **Landing — the team-size FAQ is gone**: The home page FAQ's "What team size is this built for? Does it work for one person?" is removed. The answer opened with a yes and then spent three sentences on plan limits plus a caveat that you can't invite anyone yet — pricing already carries the limits, and the caveat was the only new fact. Removed across all four locales.
- **Models — Ox Alpha on OpenRouter and Zen**: Ox Alpha is now reachable through bring-your-own-key providers — stealth/ox-alpha on OpenRouter and ox-alpha-free on Zen's Go endpoint — free while the preview runs. The model predates any pi release, so it ships as a server-side builtin patch; its three published efforts (low/high/max) map onto the endpoint's own levels, with the rest folded onto a neighbour.
- **Models — a gateway that only takes the official client is named**: Some Anthropic-compatible gateways fingerprint their caller and refuse anything that isn't the official Claude Code client with a 400. That text matched no rule and landed in "unknown", so the provider sheet and the run bubble both dumped raw JSON — one user read "upgrade your Claude Code client" out of the gateway's own words and spent a build upgrading the CLI on two machines, which couldn't help, since the request is the platform's. It's now classified provider_client_rejected: the hint says plainly that your API key and Base URL are both fine, and points at another provider or the endpoint's operator — and the add/edit provider sheets show that remedy at config time, not only after a run fails.
- **Models — OAuth providers no longer report "model unavailable"**: An OAuth-connected provider (like xAI) used to ship only the credential and leave the model definition to the executor's own pi builtin table — the one the installed CLI was published with, which runs behind this server — so a correctly configured xAI team saw "Configured model xai/grok-4.6 is unavailable on this machine". The full definition now ships wherever the wire can carry it, with only two fallbacks left on the old path: providers whose filterModels hook registerProvider would bypass (github-copilot), and an API the wire shape can't carry (openai-codex).
- **Diffs — raster images preview in the cards**: A raster image in the change review used to end at an inert "Binary files ... differ" line, since a binary patch has no body. The diff cards now reuse the file browser's raw-route pipeline: an expanded image card paints the image itself — the head ref for added/modified/renamed, the merge base for removed — instead of a placeholder line.
- **Files — an unpreviewable file gets a card**: A binary, an oversized blob, or an Office format used to end at one grey sentence that told the reader nothing they didn't already know. It now paints an identity card — type glyph, file name, format badge, size, and a filled download button — and the attachment viewer's own dead end goes through the same component. The download action moved into FileSource, so the two hosts that never had one (the todo's artifact pane and the /file screen) can offer it too, and the repo browser takes the size straight off the tree it already fetched. The copy also stops claiming the file is binary — the server only NUL-sniffs the first 8000 chars, which a UTF-16 source trips and a .docx never reaches — so all four locales now say "no preview" instead.
- **Chat — racing chief sends converge instead of a 409**: Two race windows bounced a chief message back with a toast — a send while a turn was still assembling or running (the client's SSE view lagging the server), and a steer landing just as a turn ended. Both now converge server-side: open a turn if the chief is idle, otherwise fold the message into the live turn as a steer, retrying across the ~700ms assembly window. Build conversations keep their 409, since opening a build turn is a phase transition only the build steps route can decide.
- **Chat — a lone tilde no longer strikes out half a paragraph**: GFM opens a strikethrough on a single `~`, and Chinese prose writes numeric ranges with it ("78~124步"). Two ranges in one paragraph paired up and struck out everything between them, swallowing any `**` in the way so bold painted as literal asterisks. Only `~~` now marks a deletion; a lone `~` falls through to the other inline rules and stays text.
- **Chat — quieter ref cards and a wider todo preview**: Project/skill/machine hover cards drop their footer "open …↗" link — the chip itself navigates, so the link was a second door to the same room. The todo hover card widens from 256px to 360px with the spec excerpt cut to three lines, so the card stays a glance and the panel is the read. The context-window meter previews its read-out on desktop hover, with a click still opening the modal that can compact. The mention picker shows skeleton rows and a skeleton count while skills/machines/projects/agents are still fetching, instead of painting "nothing here" over a request still in flight.
- **Notifications — a failed chief turn reads as an error, not raw text**: A failed chief turn's inbox row and lock screen used to carry whatever the failing layer said verbatim — a gateway's raw JSON, git's stderr — so a quota failure arrived as `402: {"message":"Insufficient Balance"…}`. They now classify with the same rules as the in-thread notice and render the same run_error copy in the recipient's locale; "unknown" keeps its raw text, as the bubble does.

## 2026-08-22

- **Billing — a downgraded team no longer sees a pool it can't spend**: After downgrading from Pro to Free, the plans page kept showing a full credit dashboard — meter, usage breakdown and top-up/convert buttons — describing an allowance the team no longer had, and the old trial grant left in the ledger read back as a spendable balance. Entitlement is now settled against the plan first: a plan with no pool shows only the top-up balance it actually bought (when there is one), and the dashboard and buttons fold away. Top-up balance also carries forward correctly — a renewal used to zero it despite the checkout copy always promising it would survive — and now rolls across monthly windows, renewals and downgrades alike, with the refund-dedup list carried alongside so money is never deducted twice.
- **Notifications — an account-wide push switch**: Push notifications could only be toggled per device before, and signing out on web wrote a local flag that killed browser push permanently with no way back. The account page now has one account-wide switch: turning it off applies to every device (stored server-side, on by default, no permission prompt on toggle), and the old web local flag is gone, so a sign-out and sign-in re-subscribes the browser automatically. The device's own OS permission, when denied, shows separately and still links straight to system settings.
- **Notifications — a chief reply now pushes**: When a chief finished a turn (answering you, or a proactive wake report), nothing appeared in the inbox or as a push — you had to return to the conversation to see it. Every finished turn now raises a notification with a body snippet, coalesced to a single row per chief (consecutive turns refresh the same row instead of stacking the inbox), and tapping it lands on that team's chief conversation; the banner suppresses itself while you're already looking at it. iOS push taps that failed to deep-link are fixed as part of this.
- **Memory — expiring entries and budget feedback**: An agent's memory only had one mode, keep forever, so short-lived state — an overnight authorization, a pin that only holds until the next deploy — had to be saved as never-expiring and left to stale the context. save_memory now takes an expiresAt: past that moment the entry stops being injected and is cleaned up on the next save or delete. Every save or delete also reports the current entry count and the share of the inject budget used, nudging a consolidation at 80% so the agent prunes before it's forced to at the cap.
- **Models — custom models can declare a thinking-level cap**: A bring-your-own-key model had only a reasoning on/off toggle, with no way to state the endpoint's thinking-effort ceiling — picking a level past it either got refused or silently clamped. Turning reasoning on now lets you declare "up to high/xhigh/max", registered to what the endpoint actually supports; the discovery failure for local/LAN addresses also now says plainly why it can't be probed.
- **Files — the branch picker is rebuilt**: The files page's branch picker mixed its rows — conv branches were labelled by their todo, plain branches showed only a bare name, and there was no sign of when each branch last changed. Every row is now the same shape: branch name, its todo underneath ("-" for branches with none), and its last commit time on the right — both lines searchable, with placeholder rows while loading instead of a blank.
- **Chief — every turn it starts is auto-watched**: After the chief ran a review, confirmation or merge, the only safety net was a "remember to watch" reminder in the result — which the model ignored in the wild, leaving the turn parked with no watcher to wake. It is now structural: those actions auto-create the watch (a repeat only refreshes its reason), so the chief is woken when the todo parks or settles, without leaning on prompt discipline.
- **Chief — a send and a wake no longer open two turns**: When a user sent the chief a message at the same moment a wake arrived, two concurrent turns could open, both answering the same message and each acting on it. A conversation now claims its one turn slot atomically — the idle check and the enqueue share a mutex, so whether a turn is running or still being enqueued, only one runs.
- **Agent tools — errors now hand agents a way to self-correct**: Many tool failures returned a single generic line, so an agent could only retry verbatim and burn round trips. Failures now carry actionable context: web_fetch's invalid URLs, timeouts (naming the budget) and non-2xx pages (prefixed with the HTTP status) read as what they are; resolving a machine by name lists every candidate with its id on a duplicate or a miss; and a missing todo, project, agent or skill names the id and points at the listing tool — so the agent fixes the call in one go.
- **What's new — unread is no longer read into oblivion**: The what's-new dialog used to advance the "read" cursor even when dismissed by backdrop or back gesture, and a device-local mirror swallowed entries the server had correctly ruled unread — so announcements quietly reached nobody who'd actually looked. Now only the footer button advances the cursor and the local mirror is gone; a misfire costs one repeat dialog rather than eating the announcement.
- **Notifications — markdown stripped out of push bodies**: The push snippet for an agent message or chief reply carried markdown verbatim onto the lock screen — `[#361](todo:…)` links, bold and code fences that neither a lock screen nor an inbox row can render. The snippet now strips the markup before truncating, so the lock screen reads clean text.
- **Chat — repaint immediately on returning to the foreground**: Coming back from the background (or a bfcache restore) used to wait for a heartbeat frame before repainting, leaving the conversation briefly stuck on its old frame. Returning now checks the wall clock against the last frame first — still fresh, leave it alone; otherwise reconnect at once, no heartbeat wait.
- **Attachments — image uploads compress harder**: Uploads only checked dimensions before, so a PNG screenshot within the 1568px long edge shipped raw, spending bandwidth on bytes the model gains nothing from. Byte size is now checked too, and over-limit images are re-encoded before upload; the three knobs (long-edge cap, JPEG quality, as-is threshold) are shared config across platforms.
- **Account — the web page no longer points at itself**: The "use the web app" hint and the version/OTA build line used to render on the web account page too — the hint pointing at the very page it sat on. Both lines now show only on native.

## 2026-08-21

- **App — important changes are announced in a what's-new dialog**: The product ships near-daily, but its only record was /docs/changelog — an engineering ledger of five to fifteen paragraph-long entries a day that nobody opens. Features landed and the people they were built for never heard. A curated counterpart now exists: content/whats-new holds the few changes worth stopping someone for, one file per entry across all four locales, and publishing is just dropping the files in — no id to register, no code to touch. A major entry opens the dialog on the next visit to a workspace that could actually use the feature; a minor one only lights a dot on the user menu and waits to be opened. Read state lives on the account rather than the device, so a new account starts caught up to its own signup instead of opening on the entire archive.
- **Notifications — gate and failure notices are time-sensitive**: iOS delivers the default interruption level quietly under Focus and never lights a locked screen, so a build parked at a gate could sit unseen for hours. plan_ready, build_review and build_failed now ship at the time-sensitive level, backed by the matching entitlement. Everything else keeps the default on purpose — the level is one the user can switch off per app, and it goes off for all of them at once, so spending it on an agent's own message or a billing notice costs the notifications that need it.
- **Machines — pages surface the machineId agents dispatch by**: The machine pages showed and copied deviceId — the enrollment fingerprint, which nothing outside enrollMachine reads. Pasted anywhere it might matter (a tool call, a support thread) it resolved to nothing. They now show Machine.id instead: whole on the detail row, last 8 characters in the list and chat card subtitles. The chief's machines roster had the mirror gap — names only — and now carries (machineId: …) on each line, the way agents already write them.
- **Models — backport DeepSeek's vision model**: deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp shipped on 2026-08-21 and pi 0.84.1 predates it, so a team on its own DeepSeek key had no way to select the one model of theirs that reads images. It is now backported: everything but input matches pi's deepseek-v4-flash row (DeepSeek states the two are on par on text and bills them alike), at the off-peak rates. Managed inference is untouched, so the credit pool is not spent on an experimental model.
- **Models — non-ASCII credentials are rejected up front**: An API key or custom header pasted with non-ASCII content in it — a gateway console's "线路…" label copied along with the token — was stored verbatim and only failed at build time, where undici throws an unreadable TypeError that names a string offset rather than the field. Every write path (provider create/update/discover, MCP http headers) now validates, so the paste is refused up front, and the runtime error is classified as provider_credential_not_ascii so rows saved before this rule reach a remedy instead of the raw throw — classification happens at render, so existing failures pick it up without a migration. MCP stdio env keeps the wider charset, since it is spawned into a process rather than sent as a header.
- **Chief — gate-park wakes are coalesced and shortened**: A batch dispatch parks its todos seconds apart, and each park used to spend a whole chief turn — the first wake enqueued immediately, the siblings were skipped while that turn ran and bought a follow-up turn of their own. Gate-park wakes now wait out a trailing debounce so siblings fold into one coalesced wake (settles, failed review rounds and timed check-ins still deliver at once), and the window was shortened from 30s/90s to 10s/30s — the wait between parking and hearing about it dropped from about a minute to about ten seconds. The chief also now reads the outputs before speaking, instead of opening with a placeholder acknowledgement no one is waiting for.
- **Chief — run_builds accepts hoisted dispatch options**: A chief spent a day unable to start any unassigned todo — it emitted every per-item option hoisted to the top level, where the schema dropped them, and once that malformed call was in its context it copied it verbatim on all 35 retries. The flat shape is now accepted: the option set is one literal, shared by the item schema and the top level, where it reads as a batch default. And when no item resolves an agent, the error carries the exact JSON shape plus the team's agentIds, so the model can fix the call without another read.
- **Agent tools — a notification can be marked urgent**: notify_user gains an urgent flag, letting an agent mark a notification urgent when work has stopped until the user acts — breaking through Do Not Disturb and lighting a locked screen. The default stays at the ordinary level, and it drives one send only, leaving the notification's stored document and mapping unchanged.

## 2026-08-20

- **Machines — a restarted proxy client no longer takes the whole machine down**: The daemon read the macOS system proxy once at startup and pinned it into the environment and the fetch agent, then never again; a proxy client (Clash, Surge, a corporate VPN) that restarts on a fresh loopback port therefore took the machine fully offline until the process restarted — model calls failed with "Connection error", git push with "Couldn't connect to server", and the heartbeat stopped, so the machine read offline with the computer plainly on. Some users answered with a cron running `tds restart` every 30 minutes, which then cut their own builds in half. A failing heartbeat and a model auto-retry now re-read the system proxy and, when it moved, swap both channels that carry it in place — the environment every git subprocess inherits, and the dispatcher behind globalThis.fetch — while a proxy you pinned in the environment stays yours for the whole process. The model-retry budget also rises from pi's stock 3 attempts (~14s) to 7 (~4 minutes), so an unattended build no longer dies outright on a transient network blip.
- **Builds — turns longer than an hour no longer die on credential expiry at push time**: A turn has no time cap but its claim-time credential does — GitHub caps installation tokens at 1 hour, so every ≥60-minute step's end-of-turn push was dying on "authentication required". The fix is two layers: platform conversation grants now mint with a 24-hour TTL (self-issued, no external ceiling), and the executor re-mints an expired credential once and retries the push, skipping the already-done lease seeding. The mid-turn push tool and the end-of-turn push share one credential instance, so a refresh on either path serves both. The turn's completion now also carries a structured push outcome (success, or an error with its kind and whether a stale-lease retry ran), and merge turns report push failures the same way instead of burying them in a generic error.
- **Billing — converting a trial early revokes the scheduled cancellation**: A subscription carrying a scheduled cancellation truncated the post-trial cycle into a partial period, whose charge is a proration that "none" swallows — so convert-now opened the full monthly pool, recorded the conversion, and never billed a cent. Clearing the cancellation in the same update now restores the full new cycle, so Stripe invoices and charges immediately (converting is the stronger signal, so it supersedes the scheduled cancellation).

## 2026-08-19

- **Files — an HTML preview's own links and buttons lead somewhere**: The preview iframe ran on allow-scripts alone, so every "open in a new tab" button inside a rendered document was dropped where it stood — no tab, no error, just a console line the reader never sees — and a page reached from a preview had no scripts at all, so anything that draws itself in JavaScript arrived blank. Popups are now allowed and escape the sandbox they came from, so what lands in the tab is a page rather than another scriptless frame, and HTML joins PDF and media in getting allow-scripts from the raw route — still an opaque origin, with no cookie, storage or embedder DOM within reach. A link to another repo file goes up to the host instead of navigating the frame, and the files browser reopens the target as the file it is, keeping a back/forward trail through them; outside links become a new tab at the click itself. Preview tokens last an hour and re-mint a minute before they lapse, so a document the reader is still on no longer turns into a wall of 401s.
- **Files — the HTML preview loads straight off the raw route**: A served file's preview iframe now points at the raw route itself instead of a rebuilt blob, so the document has a real URL — location and query are meaningful, fragments and GET forms work, and relative resources resolve without an injected `<base>`. A sha-pinned file also gets the route's immutable caching. The navigation shim rides on the response (a no-op opened top-level, its ROOT derived from its own location), and the HTML response's CSP keeps the popup and form tokens the frame's sandbox grants — the two intersect, so dropping them server-side would silently kill external links.
- **Chat — a table too wide for the phone pans instead of stacking**: Columns were pure shares of the bubble whatever they held — eleven of them on a 390pt screen left each about 30pt, and every cell became a column of single characters; wrapping stops rescuing a table somewhere past eight columns. When the columns' natural widths now add up to more than the bubble can give, the grid states that width and rides in a horizontal scroller; when they fit, the old proportional fill runs untouched, so desktop and every narrow table are unchanged.
- **Chat — a table's header reads as a label, not its first row**: The header carried the body's colour, and the weight set for it never reached the text — a cell's fragments spell out `fontWeight: '400'`, and the innermost declaration wins, so a column name came out identical to the number beneath it, with position the only thing separating them. It now takes the treatment the app's section labels take — tertiary, medium, letter-spaced — and the underline moves to the stronger rule so it divides labels from data.
- **Chat — a miscounted delimiter row no longer loses the table**: GFM sizes a table by its delimiter row, which only counts when it holds exactly as many cells as the header. A build agent's seven-day report wrote eleven column names under twelve alignment cells, so the whole block fell back to a paragraph and painted as ten lines of literal pipes — in the bubble, and in the markdown file the same turn committed. The repair pass now trims or pads a delimiter sitting directly under a header it doesn't match — the one position where a wrong width is a miscount rather than an intent worth guessing at — and the cells past the header's width are alignment spellings, never text, so nothing a reader would have seen is dropped.
- **Landing — the hero's subtitle defines the product**: The headline keeps its claim — the agent team that gets things done — and the line under it stops restating the collaboration pitch to define the thing instead: Todos is a minimal agent workspace, making working with agents more efficient, easier and more delightful. All four locales in step.
- **Landing — the chief's dispatch drawn the way the stream draws it**: The hero demo's proposal card — checkboxes, avatars, live phase pills — mocked a UI the product no longer has. A multi-todo dispatch is now the stream's own two-column table: todo chip and title, agent chip (face and name), the header set as a section label over a strong rule. A single-todo dispatch skips the table, its todo and agent chips riding inline in the chief's sentence.

## 2026-08-18

- **Attachments — every file opens in a viewer**: An attachment chip used to do one useful thing — open an image — while a PDF, spreadsheet, or Markdown note fell through to the browser, and because its signed URL is served as a download by design, clicking one only saved the file. The chip also sat inert while its URL loaded and went dead five minutes later when the signed link expired. A chip is now always clickable, and what opens is one viewer for everything, rendering PDFs, Markdown and text through the file browser's own renderers; Office formats, which no browser can render, say so and offer a download instead of an empty frame. The signed URL is minted at the moment of use, so an expired link costs one request on the next click rather than a dead chip, and every document chip on desktop now has a hover card naming its type, size and age.
- **Machines — the online dot tells the truth, and an offline machine is answered in the thread**: The green presence dot was whatever the last list fetch happened to catch, so a machine that shut down stayed green until something unrelated refreshed it. Presence now carries a real online flag with the same 60-second lease Redis keeps, and the client tracks that lease itself — the dot turns grey on its own when a machine stops beating, no refresh needed, while a steady heartbeat stays silent instead of re-rendering every screen. The other half: a turn that lands on a machine that is off no longer queues into a dead queue and shows "waking machine…" for ten minutes. It now fails immediately, with the reason in the thread; only a sleeping hosted machine is still woken rather than refused.
- **Agents — role and skills on the page you land on**: The two facts that answer "who is this agent" — the role description injected into every one of its turns, and the skills it always carries — lived behind a "role" tab most people never opened. They now sit on the overview tab you land on, which splits into an identity card (face, name, role, skills) and a config card (model, thinking). The tab bar drops from four to three, with memory now ahead of access.
- **Agents — a memory row says where it came from and when**: The memory list discarded most of what the route already handed it — an entry's project was reduced to the bare word "project", the time it was added went unused, and the update time showed only for non-admins. Each row now ends with a metadata line naming the project it belongs to (a chip that opens that project) and when it was added and last updated. A search box and a sort menu now ride above the list, and a read that fails says so instead of flattening into "this agent has learned nothing".
- **Chat — a turn reports the memory it changed**: An agent curating its own memory left no trace where anyone was looking — save_memory returned a line into the model's context and stopped there. A turn that touches memory now ends with one system notice counting what it added, changed and removed, linking the agent's memory tab. Counts rather than titles, and one notice rather than one per call, so a consolidation that rewrites an entry and drops three near-duplicates reads as one thing the agent did, not four rows.
- **Chat — a path on the agent's disk is no longer dressed up as a link**: An agent that names its delivery by the path it wrote it to handed the renderer a bare absolute path, which the browser resolved against the page it sat on — the link read todos.dev/Users/… and opened a 404 for a file the product never held. Such paths have no address to give, so they stop pretending to be links and draw as the path itself, whole and ready to copy into a terminal or Finder window.
- **Chief — the check-ins it promised, next to what it watches**: set_wake let the chief arm a timed check-in, but nothing showed one — the only trace was a line inside a tool result, so a promise set for the wrong hour, or forgotten, was invisible until it landed or didn't. The chief's watching tab now holds both under their own headings: the todos it subscribed to, and the pending check-ins it armed (a delivered one is deleted, so only pending ones appear). Times read as today/tomorrow plus the clock, and each note renders its todo chips as tappable links.
- **GitHub — a taken account gets a way out instead of a dead end**: An account belongs to one team at a time, and the refusal used to say only that — the advice people got was to start over. The conflict now names who holds the account: when that is a team you administer, the page offers to disconnect it and retries your login for you; otherwise it points at GitHub, where uninstalling the app is the authoritative release. Team settings also gains an account list, so a dead installation that can no longer mint a token can still be listed and released.

## 2026-08-17

- **Files — preview PDF and media files**: The Files page now renders PDF and media files inline, the way it already renders images and markdown. A PDF opens in the built-in viewer — on web it avoids Chrome's sandboxed-plugin block by relying on the raw route's own content-security policy rather than an iframe sandbox attribute, which Chrome refuses to load its PDF viewer in — while HTML previews keep the sandbox they genuinely need.
- **Chat — LaTeX math renders in messages**: Formulas written with the standard delimiters — `\(...\)`, `\[...\]`, `$$...$$`, `$...$` — now render as real math instead of being mangled by markdown. A `\(t\)` used to read as escaped punctuation and paint as `(t)`, and a display formula whose own line held a lone `=` could be promoted into a heading. Inline math renders as text with real sub- and superscripts; display math — fractions, roots, matrices — stacks in boxes and scrolls sideways; and anything the parser can't read stays visible as its own source, so a formula degrades one span at a time.
- **Builds — the end-of-turn push is synchronous, and failures surface end to end**: A build no longer reports success while its branch is still stuck on the machine. The end-of-turn push used to be deferred and best-effort — a corporate proxy or a flaky push to GitHub could fail silently, and the Chief would announce completion with a Files link that never left the machine. The push is now synchronous, its real outcome (pushed or failed) rides on the turn's finish, failures are written as notices in the thread, the Files page shows a "not pushed" state, and the next turn's prompt carries any pending failure so the agent answers delivery questions honestly.
- **Builds — fix-evidence demand off human feedback rounds**: Fixed a human reviewer's one-line ask drawing the same per-point evidence requirement as an unattended critique — re-reading every fixed location and quoting the updated text back. That requirement exists to break an unattended review-revision loop with no human in it, but the wait it buys landed on the reviewer already watching the diff. The block now keys on the same reviewer signal, so human feedback rounds are spared while reviewer rounds and mixed backlogs are unchanged.
- **Models — DeepSeek's 2026-08-17 repricing**: DeepSeek moved to a two-band sheet on 17 August, and the credit ledger now follows it. A typical task now draws 282 credits on V4 Flash and 847 on V4 Pro — buying 124 and 41 tasks against the Pro pool — instead of the previous 232 and 77.
- **Chief — report each machine's tds version and name the ones behind**: The Chief's machine roster now lists each machine's tds version, and a machine of your own running behind npm's latest says so and hands over the upgrade commands. Before this the roster only spoke up when a CLI fell below the floor that can't take a step at all — everything between that floor and the published release read exactly like a machine installed this morning. A platform machine reports its version but is never handed upgrade commands, since its CLI ships inside the platform's own image.
- **Chief — name the tool call an in-flight turn is stuck inside**: A turn wedged inside one long tool call emitted nothing at all, and the Chief read it as a slow plan — a 16-minute recursive grep looked exactly like a model that hadn't replied yet. The Chief now names the tool call, with the command itself, so a wedged grep is told apart from a legitimate long build.
- **Chief — refuse a model switch the conversation no longer fits**: Switching to a model with a smaller context window no longer silently strands the conversation. Once the conversation sits at or above the new ceiling it can neither run a turn nor compact its way back, so the settings page now weighs the incoming model's window against the last measured occupancy and refuses the switch outright, pointing at a compaction or a rewind instead.
- **Chief — route a delivery that never landed to the machine's tds version**: When a todo reads done but the Files page is empty, the Chief now checks the machine's tds version before reaching for the repository or the agent. Below 0.1.48 the end-of-turn push was deferred and best-effort and reported neither outcome, so the machine that needs the upgrade is the one machine that cannot say so. Two counter-cases keep the upgrade from becoming the answer to everything: a platform machine's CLI ships inside its image, and a thread already showing "Branch push failed" is new enough to report one.
- **Chat — name the machine each turn runs on**: Build and Chief threads now open on a "Running on <machine>" notice, with the name linking to that machine — written only when the machine differs from the previous turn, so a long thread doesn't repeat one unchanging fact every turn. A pinned pick says so instead, and a mid-turn reroute announces itself too.
- **Chat — hover cards for skill and machine chips**: A skill or machine named in a message was the only kind of chip a desktop pointer learned nothing from. Both now show hover cards — the machine card carries presence, the shell and build-off badges and the concurrency cap, drawn the same way the machines list draws them. Chips of these two kinds also follow a rename, the way project chips do.
- **Chat — label links instead of pasting bare addresses**: A Files link carrying a Chinese filename arrives percent-encoded, and pasted bare it filled four lines of the bubble with escape codes. The Chief and build prompts now wrap every URL in a labelled markdown link, and the renderer collapses an autolinked bare address to its host plus the decoded name it points at. The href is untouched, and the host stays in front so a shortened link still says where it goes.
- **Chat — links are real anchors on web**: A link in the stream was a Text with a click handler, which web rendered as a span — no copy-address in the context menu, no hover preview, no middle-click. It now renders as a real anchor: outward links open in a new tab, and in-app links route through the app while a modified click is left to the browser.
- **Merge — a diverged branch gets honest guidance**: A merge turn whose remote branch had diverged was rejected seven times over ninety minutes with the same git error — and every click invited "Click Done to retry", which runs the identical code against the identical state. A diverged branch now says what is on the remote, that nothing was pushed or overwritten, and that a person has to settle the branch first.
- **Merge — a missing merge head reports ref_not_found**: When a GitHub merge's build branch never actually landed, the failure was being folded into the generic "check the repository connection and permissions" guidance. It now surfaces as ref_not_found, which says what is true — the remote branch is missing, so Done re-pushes and retries.
- **CLI v0.1.48**: Checkpoint pushes and the push_branch tool now bypass the repository's own pre-push hooks — a hook written for a developer's machine (a test gate needing a TTY, a prepare script setting core.hooksPath) could fail opaquely and kill every conversation's checkpoint push on that machine with a bare "failed to push some refs".

## 2026-08-16

- **Billing — buy Pro with WeChat Pay as a prepaid term**: Pro is now purchasable as a one-off prepaid term. Stripe only carries WeChat Pay in Checkout's payment mode — subscription and setup modes are refused — so WeChat Pay users previously had no route onto Pro at all. The prepaid term is priced in CNY; one payment upgrades the team to Pro until it expires and renews nothing by itself. Card subscriptions are untouched, and the two sources stay mutually exclusive. Refunds — the only clawback signal WeChat Pay has — are now handled: a refunded term downgrades, a refunded top-up is reversed, and staff are mailed either way.
