Buying reads as one decision: each payment method carries its own price with a single pay button beneath. Trial-eligible teams lead with the card whatever the language; otherwise Chinese leads with WeChat. Language only ranks the options — both stay reachable.
- **Machines — pin builds, chief turns and schedules to a named machine**: A build, the chief conversation, or a schedule rule can now bind to one team machine. Every turn queues on it — offline queues rather than falling back — and ineligibility (removed, builds off, stale CLI, exhausted credits) fails with a reasoned error instead of silently rerouting. Pickers in the start sheet, schedule modal and chief settings list build-enabled machines with live presence, and the chief's tools accept a machineId when the user names one.
- **Schedules — each rule's machine, project and outcome at a glance**: Schedule rows are no longer four grey lines. Each now leads with a clock plate and the rhythm, then one meta line: the next run (e.g. "Today 09:00"), the pinned machine with its presence dot, and the project. A pin that no longer resolves to a build-capable machine turns amber — that rule fails every cycle until repinned. Cycle outcomes carry tone too: amber for quota and agent skips, red for a failed start, grey for an ordinary busy skip.
- **Schedules — skip a cycle when no machine can take it**: A machine that stays offline no longer costs one dead build per cycle. The sweep used to fire regardless, park the step on the offline machine's queue, and get cleaned up ten minutes later — one team's hourly rule burned sixteen builds in a single seventeen-hour outage, crowding the parallel slots and making its other schedules report "quota full". A cycle now checks for an online, eligible machine first and records a "skipped offline" outcome otherwise. Notifications also fire on an outcome change rather than once per bad cycle, so one outage no longer means one identical email per hour.
- **Chief — settled todos on the board**: The chief todo page's "done" and "closed" filters were always empty — two layers removed terminal rows before the filter saw them. Both filters now work, while the default view (no phase selected = open only) is unchanged. The progress ring also gets its own lighter endpoint returning the open count and a small preview, so it no longer grows heavier as history accrues.
- **Chief — notices when tool definitions change**: The chief now detects changes to tool definitions and opens the first turn after a drift with a factual notice naming the added, changed and removed tools. Previously a long conversation could anchor on its own earlier statements about tool parameters — in production a chief once insisted a newly added parameter didn't exist.
- **Home — two selling points replace three repeated sections**: The first three selling points replayed the hero's own story — the chief splitting an ask, models per seat, progress reported back — three screens of scrolling with nothing new. They give way to two the hero never covers: the roster nobody configured, and a round whose branches converge — with parallel delivery now framed as a round costing its slowest todo rather than the sum of them.
- **Login — a failed lookup no longer signs you out**: Fixed transient user-lookup failures being read as "no such user" and answered with a 401 — clients obey a 401 by signing out, and during payment activation that bounced between the activation and setup screens. A failed lookup now answers 503 instead, so a transient failure no longer signs the user out.
- **App — returning no longer cold-boots**: Fixed returning to the app still re-running the full cold boot. A page kept a streaming request open while hidden, and Chrome refuses to cache a page with an outstanding XHR. The stream now closes on page hide and reconnects on return, replaying anything missed.
- **Chat — stray @ removed from skill mention chips**: Fixed a skill mention rendering with a stray @ glued to the front of its chip. The skill marker was the only type that wrote its sigil outside the link brackets, so a sent message's real Markdown parse turned the @ into punctuation before the chip. The marker now keeps the @ optional, and old messages still fold and parse correctly.

## 2026-08-15

- **Onboarding — what the team is for, beside how to get one**: On a wide enough screen the onboarding page now splits in two, with a rule down the centre: a looping Chief conversation and three use-case stories on one side, the setup form itself on the other. Below that width the page is unchanged, with the three stories scrolling in a strip under the CTA.
- **Chat — multi-select in every mention category**: The mention picker now multi-selects in every category — skills, agents, projects and machines, not just todos — so picking two agents no longer means opening the picker twice. A tap toggles each item, and the footer commits them all in one insert.
- **Chat — composer prompt library retired**: The prompt-library button and its modal are gone. New teams still get the four getting-started goals, now shown in the Chief's empty state.
- **Chat — detached steers share one footer**: Steers picked up by an auto-started turn now group under a single turn footer, so a run of them carries one copy button instead of one per row.
- **Files — dead links redirect to the current build**: A Files link minted before a rerun now redirects to the todo's current build branch with a notice, instead of landing on a 404.
- **Billing — credit exhaustion speaks your language**: When a Pro team's credits run dry, the app now says so in your language and links straight to the plan tab to top up or end the trial early — instead of a confusing "connect a machine" message.
- **Agent tools — a read-only projects tool**: Agents gain a read-only `projects` tool that lists every project with its id, so the Chief can name a project instead of reporting it missing. The todos list no longer fills up with empty projects.
- **Chief — reviews relay your explicit ask**: When you explicitly ask for another AI review round, the Chief can now run it even after the automatic review loop hits its safety cap, instead of being turned away.
- **Merge — server-side fallback and actionable failures**: A platform-hosted merge that can't fast-forward now falls back to a server-side merge, and a failed merge now tells you what went wrong and what to do next.
- **Chief — skipped builds are named**: When a batch build start comes up empty, the Chief now names the skipped todos and the reasons, instead of a vague "no buildable todos".

## 2026-08-14

- **Use cases — a third story, told by the agent team**: The /use-cases page gains a third first-person account — a quant strategy researcher building BTC perpetual-futures strategies, where the bottleneck is verification latency rather than ideas. All three stories (indie game developer, deep-learning researcher, quant strategy researcher) now frame the work around the agent team — the lead, architect and analysts run the work while the human approves and rejects.
- **Billing — a trial now reads as TRIAL**: A seven-day Pro trial no longer shows "PRO" across the app. The plan chip now reads TRIAL in its own indigo, so you can see the clock running instead of mistaking it for a paid plan.
- **Billing — trial & payment resilience**: A card-less trial's plan tab now points at "Upgrade now" (adding a card is the fix) instead of "Manage subscription". Stripe subscription updates are re-read before applying, an hourly sweep reconciles drifted subscriptions, and a trial whose conversion charge fails keeps running on its trial limits instead of being marked past-due.
- **Chief — prompt library**: The Chief composer gains a prompt library — a two-level picker (category, then prompt) that drops a ready-made or half-written prompt into the box for you to finish. A "My prompts" list lets you save, edit and delete your own prompts (private to you, per team) alongside the curated ones. New accounts also keep the four getting-started goals here after the empty state has gone.
- **Agent tools — cancel_workflow**: Build agents can now stop an in-progress GitHub Actions run with cancel_workflow — for a run a newer push has superseded, or one stuck burning CI minutes.
- **Chat — a build's first message says what it is for**: A build's opening message now names what's starting — the todo chip and its title — instead of a bare number. Turns the reader didn't start (by the Chief or a schedule) now say who triggered them.
- **Chat — running-turn polish**: A collapsed turn's one-line peek now follows the newest activity — thinking or a tool call — instead of going stale at "connecting to model…". The elapsed counter keeps its spacing steady as the digits tick.
- **App — empty pages introduce themselves**: Skills, MCP servers, schedules, secrets and API keys now open, when empty, with an icon, a one-sentence description, the action that starts them, and a link to the docs.
- **Models — GLM-5.3 on Z.AI**: GLM-5.3 is now available on Z.AI Coding Plan connections (international and mainland China endpoints), ahead of its pi release.
- **Onboarding — setup tab remembered**: Onboarding now remembers your chosen setup tab per team, so returning to setup no longer resets you to the platform pitch.
- **UI polish**: Plan quota meters use one consistent accent colour, and lists read at the team pages' width.

## 2026-08-13

- **Models — Grok 4.6 as a managed model**: Grok 4.6 joins the managed-inference lineup, and xAI OAuth providers now pick up built-in model patches, so Grok 4.6 is available through SuperGrok / X Premium connections too.
- **Chief — secrets & project tools**: The Chief can now propose setting a team secret through an input card (the value is entered securely and never appears in chat) and deleting secrets through a confirm card. A new update_project tool lets the Chief rename projects.
- **Plan tab — preview Pro before checkout**: The plan tab now previews Pro before you commit — sandbox sizes, models, and trial notes with monthly/yearly tabs and trial vs. pay-now options side by side. Onboarding-style blurbs now explain each plan quota.
- **Billing — payment failures surfaced**: A past-due subscription now shows an amber warning on the plan tab prompting you to update your payment method, and team admins receive a payment-failed email. The credit pool is blocked while past due, and a card-less trial now lapses (ends) instead of converting when it expires. Billing notifications also land in the in-app inbox.
- **Change diffs rebuilt from Git**: Change diffs are now recomputed directly from the Git provider with lazy per-file loading, so large diffs render faster and more accurately.
- **Chat polish**: Native chat threads now run on an inverted FlatList for smoother long conversations. Streaming Markdown holds a table's header until it fully parses as a table. The working label persists during retries with an attempt count, and orphaned-tool-call errors show a clear name instead of raw JSON.
- **Decision cards auto-fold**: Cards you've decided now fold automatically, with a fold toggle and indicator so settled items stay out of the way.
- **UI polish**: Sidebar navigation and header icons gain hover tooltips. Error notices are softened and the stop button gets a tumble animation. Plan actions move to the row edge as primary buttons, and provider/machine lists align with their loading rows.
- **Welcome email**: The welcome email signature now links to the founder's X profile.
- **CLI v0.1.47**: Failed turns now checkpoint their partial work on the branch before reporting, so file changes written before a gateway error or crash survive for a resume instead of being lost.

## 2026-08-12

- **Landing page refreshed around human-agent collaboration**: The hero subtitle now frames Todos as a workspace where humans and agents work together. The hero chat demo switched from a card game to a 2D platformer (Voltrun), whose physics, collision, and boss-AI terms read unmistakably as game development. A secondary "Use cases" link now sits beside the primary CTA.
- **Use-cases — two real-user stories**: The five fictional customer stories were replaced with two first-person accounts drawn from real user sessions — an indie game developer and a deep-learning researcher — updated across all four locales.
- **Open-todo cap per project**: Each project now caps open tasks at 200; completed and closed tasks don't count. Both in-app and agent task creation show a clear, localized message when the limit is reached.
- **Todo list & Chief polish**: Project group headers with their todo counts now always display. Hovering a todo's stage ring or the Chief progress ring reveals a popover of busy todos, and the Chief now sees empty projects when listing tasks. The team machine list uses the monitor glyph with a title-side status dot (green for online and hosted sandboxes).
- **Real-time team updates**: Project and machine changes now stream to the team in real time, so rosters and settings stay current without a refresh.
- **Chat polish**: Streaming replies now reveal progressively, typewriter-style. Web chat gains a jump-to-latest button to re-pin to the newest message after scrolling up, mention chips are highlighted in the accent colour, and native chat keeps following the live stream.
- **Onboarding — cloud server tip**: The "add a machine" step now suggests preferring a cloud server, since laptops can sleep mid-build while a VPS stays up.
- **Reliability fixes**: A 15-second fetch timeout stops the app from spinning forever on a stalled request. Mobile per-user team keys are dot-separated so SecureStore accepts them, and team preferences are scoped per user so impersonating another account no longer bleeds settings across sessions.

- **Chief: time awareness — timezone, current-time line & report-back**: The Chief now receives the user's device timezone and sees a current-time line in context, enabling accurate scheduling and time-sensitive reporting. A new report-back discipline closes the loop on completed tasks so the Chief confirms outcomes rather than leaving them open-ended.
- **Chief: set_wake for off-platform follow-ups**: The Chief can schedule one-shot timed check-ins — set a wake time to follow up on work running outside the platform. The wake fires with full context of what was expected, so the Chief knows exactly what to verify when the check-in triggers.
- **Cut turns surfaced**: Turns terminated before completion (cut turns) now appear distinctly in the message bubble and are reported to the Chief, so interrupted work is visible rather than silently lost.
- **Build: abnormal stop reasons recorded**: Turn-end stop reasons — timeouts, cancellations, token exhaustion — are now recorded on runs and messages, making every non-completion traceable.
- **Sandbox: wake and driver call retry**: Sandbox wake operations and bound driver calls now retry on failure instead of failing permanently. This fixes transient errors that previously left sandboxes stuck in a broken state.
- **Chief: wake gap fixes — purge cascade, stale horizon, honest deletes**: Three fixes close Chief-wake gaps: a purge cascade ensures deleted teams don't leave orphaned wake state; stale horizon detection drops expired wake entries; and failed deletes now report truthfully instead of silently succeeding.

## 2026-08-11

- **Platform Git: merge and tag endpoints**: Platform-hosted repos now support merge and tag API endpoints, enabling automated branch-and-release workflows directly on the platform.
- **File browser: image preview**: Raster images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, etc.) now render inline in the project files browser alongside code and Markdown previews.
- **Chief: delete agents via confirm-card**: The Chief can now propose removing agents through a confirm-card flow — two-tap approval with per-agent re-authorization at decision time. Agents whose permissions have lapsed are skipped and reported instead of stranding the batch.
- **Agent tools: attachment-aware spec editing**: Spec and feedback attachments now render at their inline marker positions instead of a trailing list. Spec and steer text are gated on deliverable attachment markers, preventing stale content from surviving a spec update. Todo specs stay in sync with overriding follow-ups from the Chief. ask_user and confirm cards are deduplicated by turn-keyed document identity, preventing duplicate cards from appearing.
- **Chat: mention picker overhaul**: The mention picker now runs server-side search with multi-select for todos. Layout is denser, human members are removed, and categories are reordered for faster selection. Overflow anchoring on reversed message threads is disabled for smoother scroll behavior.
- **Conversation reads show in-flight turns**: In-progress build turns are now surfaced when agents read conversations, so the Chief and build agents see the full picture including work currently underway.
- **Build: revision turn resilience**: Revision turns now recognize duplicate and interrupted feedback rounds. A second feedback submission within the same cycle no longer silently overwrites the first. Interrupted rounds replay correctly instead of being applied incorrectly.
- **Chief: watch wake efficiency & sync spinner**: Watch wakes are slimmed down and digest churn is folded to reduce noise in Chief conversations. The Chief now tolerates dummy fields (`_`, `reason`) in tool-call arguments that previously surfaced as errors. The Chief header sync spinner now appears beside the title on both web and native.
- **UI polish batch**: The Chief sidebar icon is now a chef toque. The sidebar plan badge shrinks to a compact FREE/PRO label at the title top-right. Files and diff preview chrome moved into the page header. Plan badge styling, team page width, skills spacing, and file-preview defaults are all polished. Docs header width is aligned and onboarding chrome is tidied.

## 2026-08-10

- **Onboarding reimagined — from goal to team, no interview**: The onboarding interview is gone. State your first goal to the Chief, and the Chief immediately staffs your agent team, breaks the work into todos, and reports back. The seed now creates a single Chief-bound agent and one empty project. Activation copy updated to match. The Chief empty state shows four goal suggestion cards for unstaffed teams.
- **Pro 7-day free trial**: Pro now offers a 7-day card-required trial, once per account. While trialing you get a reduced $2/10,000-credit pool, DeepSeek-only models, 5 parallel builds, 2 machines, and 5 agents — every limit annotated in the pricing docs and UI. End the trial early anytime to unlock full Pro instantly. The onboarding offer layout is redesigned to lead with the hosted path.
- **Landing page repositioned — agent-team first**: The hero headline now leads with the agent-team positioning. The subtitle names the two things behind it: three layers of memory per agent, and a Chief that manages the team, assigns work, tracks progress, and reports results. All four locales updated.
- **Chief understands platform machines**: The Chief now distinguishes platform-hosted sandboxes from user-enrolled machines, so a Pro team whose only machine is the hosted one no longer gets told "please start a machine." The machine roster is reformatted to show kind, awake/asleep state, and credit-exhausted reason. A new platform-machines doc ships in English and Chinese; concepts, overview, and troubleshooting pages are updated.
- **Sandbox awake time is lease-based, not lock-based**: Hosted sandboxes no longer grab a keepAlive lock. Instead, every step claim and heartbeat pushes the sleep deadline one idle window out — work extends the lease, and the deadline expiring is itself the sleep decision. Fixed a bug where concurrent steps had their lock dropped early by whichever step finished first, preventing mid-turn sleep.
- **UI fixes**: Back/forward cache (bfcache) restored — returning to the app no longer cold-boots. Long screen titles truncate instead of overlapping header actions. Header side-slot presses now pass through to the title. The chat thread correctly re-pins to the bottom after the boot sync merges.

## 2026-08-09

- **AI review overhaul — context carry-forward & convergence**: Repeat review rounds no longer start from scratch. Each round now injects the prior critique and the producer's evidenced revision reply, shifting the review job from discovery to convergence — verify prior blocking points first, then review what the revision changed, and approve when nothing left genuinely gates the merge. A different reviewer (alternating specialist chains, ~10% of rounds) keeps full discovery breadth while inheriting verification duties. First-round behavior is unchanged. The circuit-breaker now tells the chief what to do next: summarize remaining blocking points for the user.
- **Chief confirm-card delete**: The chief can now propose deleting skills or todos, presenting a danger-styled confirm card that only executes when the user clicks Delete. Each item is re-authorized at decision time — team-admin for skills, ownership for todos — and items whose permissions went stale are skipped and reported instead of stranding the batch.
- **Build reliability — stranded runs & wedged claim recovery**: Runs orphaned by lost BullMQ jobs no longer hang forever at "connecting to machine" — they're now settled through the standard failure funnel with cause-specific copy for the task owner. Fixed a Node 22 bug where garbage-collected timeout signals silently wedged a machine's claim loop for an entire day; the server detects stale claims, treats the machine as offline, and sweeps its queued jobs.
- **Conversation stream self-healing & duplicate wake dedup**: The conversation SSE now reconnects automatically after a drop and recovers missed messages — no need to refresh. Duplicate chief wake turns that snuck past the index-refresh window are now deduplicated so no concurrent turns queue onto one session.
- **Decision cards auto-fold**: Question and confirm cards you've walked past now fold to a one-line summary (with the recorded picks for questions), unfolding on tap. Only your own messages count for settling — agent progress reports between pending asks leave them still active.
- **Team UI streamlined**: The team roster now shows only Add Agent; the invite-member button and modal are removed. FAQ, docs, and interface copy align across the board with the solo + agents model. Pricing and upgrade pages drop the human-members row; agent quota is labeled as a count; content columns are widened.
- **Machine deletion guard**: Machines with running tasks cannot be deleted — the endpoint returns a localized toast explaining why, preventing accidental task termination.
- **Stages popover header fixes**: The stages popover header now shows project name and sequence number (matching the task reference card layout). Fixed a desktop flash at the origin before measurement and aligned the mobile sheet header with desktop.
## 2026-08-08

- **Chief task list — watched todos & contextual suggestions**: Watched todos now appear alongside Chief-created tasks on the `/chief/todos` page for a unified view. The Chief empty state is replaced with contextual suggestion cards, making it clearer what to do next.
- **Build stream & AI review visibility**: Build turns now emit structured stage events with sequence deduplication, so progress is more reliable. Running AI reviews are surfaced as plan-reviewing and implement-reviewing phases in the todo status — no more wondering if a review is in flight.
- **Scheduled task failure alerts**: Team members now receive email notifications when a scheduled task fails, with unified channel tracking and a daily throttle to avoid noise.
- **Skills list — search, sort & import guidance**: The skills list page now supports keyword search and column sorting. The skill import page shows a Chief hint to help new users understand what skills are for.
- **Landing page — live preview & cleanup**: A new "live preview" selling point section showcases how HTML/Markdown output renders inside the file browser. Agent corner badges are removed from the demo roster for a cleaner look.
- **Welcome email redesign**: The welcome email is redesigned as a founder letter with refined copy across all locales.
- **HTML file preview — relative paths**: The file browser's HTML preview now resolves relative paths, so local assets (images, CSS, JS) render correctly inside previewed pages.
- **Schedule modal — project & todo picker**: The schedule creation modal now includes a second page for picking the target project and todo, streamlining the setup flow.
- **Hosted sandbox — proxy & Git env injection**: Hosted sandboxes now inject proxy and Git-host environment variables automatically, so agents can reach package registries and platform-hosted repos without manual config.
- **Chat & UI polish**: Collapsing a chat message now folds its thinking trace as well. The sidebar install entry is restored; review-related UI wording ("审核") is unified across the app. The StatusRing component uses element opacity for smoother rendering.
- **Build reliability — corrupt ref healing**: Git fetches wedged by corrupt local refs now heal automatically instead of failing the build.
- **ML researcher customer story**: A new machine-learning researcher use case joins the customer stories on `/use-cases`.

## 2026-08-07

- **Pro plan stabilized & quota increase**: The Pro experimental flag is removed — Pro is now stable. Agent cap raised from 10 to 15; parallel builds from 8 to 10. Pricing cards now include a built-in models comparison row; the upgrade comparison page adopts the marketing table style with a "Recommended" Pro column. Sidebar team name shows a Free/Pro badge. Full conversion-funnel tracking covers checkout, auth friction, and first-touch attribution.
- **Platform-hosted repos for Free teams**: Free teams can now create Todos-hosted repositories. Onboarding seeds a platform repo for every new user instead of falling back to an unbound project. The pricing comparison table shows a limited-time amber clock icon for the Free column instead of a disabled cross.
- **Chief todo list & badge**: The Chief header now shows an incomplete-task count badge that links to a dedicated `/chief/todos` page. All Chief-created tasks display grouped by project, with list and grid view support.
- **Chief reliability fixes**: Fixed the Chief status ring spinning indefinitely after a merge landed — todo rows now render from live snapshots so terminal transitions reflect instantly. Rewound-span digest events are now labeled as first-sight so the model presents them as new information rather than remembered state. Late-arriving digest lines now carry the live phase stamp so the Chief never contradicts its own wake data. New bounded-recovery sweeps: lost todo-watch wakes re-drain every 5 minutes; turns half-finalized by a server crash are detected and settled within a minute, surfacing the error to the task owner.
- **Build reliability**: A stream idle watchdog now rewrites silent provider stalls into retryable errors — 300s timeout for the first event, 120s between subsequent events — so stuck model streams trigger an auto-retry instead of hanging. Git clone/fetch operations killed by timeouts now show "Retrying m/n" status frames instead of appearing hung at "Preparing." Fixed a review dead-end where builds whose changes were made entirely over remote_shell (producing no diff document) triggered infinite retry loops.
- **Agent avatar customization**: Agent detail pages now include a face picker — choose from a preset style grid, upload a photo, or reset to default. Click any avatar for a 200px preview. The team members page defaults to list layout with a chart/list toggle that remembers your preference locally.
- **UI polish**: The Chief badge and todo phase ring now share a single StatusRing component — running tasks show a brand-colored comet-tail spinner; at rest a soft-tint badge. The todo header close button is restored on desktop; the phase ring stroke is thickened for readability. iOS: fixed CJK button labels sitting ~1pt low and primary button text not vertically centered.

## 2026-08-06

- **Pro plan quota rebalance**: Monthly credits increased from 30,000 to 35,000, with a proportional bump in purchasable sandbox hours per size (Small/Medium/Large now buy 102/71/44 hours). Pro drops to 3 members and 4 machines (one of which is the platform-hosted machine); storage lowered to 20 GB. Free drops to 1 machine — enough for a single laptop to try everything.
- **Agent cap & schedule limit**: Plan-tiered agent caps — Free max 5, Pro max 10. Schedule limit lowered from 50 to 10. The plan settings page now shows an agent usage meter, and the create-agent flow surfaces a localized error when the cap is hit.
- **Credit top-up & pool breakdown**: Pro teams can now top up credits. The credit usage panel shows a pool allocation breakdown. Fixed thread scroll-to-bottom.
- **File viewer syntax highlighting**: The file browser now supports syntax highlighting and preview for a variety of programming languages.
- **Hosted sandbox refinements**: The hosted machine page now shows a sleep countdown; idle timeout unified to 10 minutes. The sandbox image now ships the tds-tunnel binary for remote shell support. Sandbox deploys now drain instead of killing workers; superseded backups are deleted instead of kept for a month.
- **Plan guidance polish**: Upgrade page, provider overview, and machine banner guidance copy has been reworked throughout. The upgrade page fixes a Stripe return URL and adds a payment-verifying state, plus layout and CTA polish.
- **Preparation progress visible**: Pre-thinking preparation is now surfaced as thinking content so users aren't left staring at a blank wait.
- **Delete safeguard warnings**: Deleting an agent or machine now warns when removal leaves no room to add one back, preventing accidental lock-out.
- **Builder scheduling**: Execution targets now filter out builders without a tunnel, avoiding wasted assignments.
- **Qwen model backport**: qwen3.8-max backported onto Qwen Token Plan providers.
- **Todo header with phase ring**: The avatar stack in the todo header is replaced by a phase ring icon and stages popover for at-a-glance status.
- **Terms update**: Updated terms of service and privacy policy for hosted machines, hosted Git, and Pro.

## 2026-08-05

- **Pro plan with credits & hosted sandboxes**: A credit-metered Pro plan launches at $19/month ($15.20/month billed annually) with 30,000 monthly credits per team. Credits are denominated at our fixed cost of $0.0002 each, drawn down by hosted-machine awake time and managed inference — and stop, never overbill, when exhausted. Each Pro team gets one resizable platform-hosted sandbox (Small/Medium/Large), billed by awake hour. The managed-inference gateway fronts DeepSeek V4 Flash, V4 Pro, GPT-5.6 Luna, and Grok Build 0.1 / 4.3 / 4.5 — six models metered per call at what they cost us. BYOK inference is permanently free and unmetered on every plan. Onboarding and billing UI ships alongside for plan purchase and credit tracking.
- **Pricing page & billing copy polish**: Simplified the marketing pricing section; aligned credit wording. The cancellation FAQ now reflects a 15-day over-limit grace period. Yearly total moved next to the plan-tab upgrade button.

## 2026-08-04

- **Repo file browser**: Every project now has a "Files" tab — browse platform and GitHub repository trees, switch branches and commit snapshots, view and download files, all inside the app. Upload and delete files directly; each operation commits to the branch head. The old worktree sync surface is retired; all code output now flows through the file browser.
- **CLI v0.1.46**: Termux (Android) support — the tunnel binary now ships and runs on Android. Fixed DNS resolution failures on environments without /etc/resolv.conf that prevented the tunnel from starting.
- **In-app deep links**: Links agents hand out — the Files page, a task's panel — now open inside the app instead of an external browser. iOS Universal Links are live, so tapping a Todos link anywhere launches the app.
- **Question card reliability**: Fixed an issue where some models omitted the reference marker after calling ask_user, leaving the question card invisible to the user. Previously ~15% of questions (118 cards) went unreferenced and unseen; missing markers are now backfilled automatically so every question card renders.
- **Sync mount deduplication & fault tolerance**: One mirror per machine per task — no more duplicate mounts. Unusable destinations are retired on the first failure with a clear notice to the task owner instead of retrying indefinitely.
- **Tunnel status visibility**: The machine page now reports why the tunnel is down, not just that it is. The Chief reads this to name the real remote-shell blocker instead of suggesting phantom fixes when the tunnel is at fault.
- **Prompt streamlining**: Code-access guidance unified per audience; per-turn note accumulation eliminated, saving ~470 characters per turn. Agent file links now point directly to the file, not just the branch.

## 2026-08-03

- **Context meter**: A context-window meter with absolute token counts now sits in the chat header. A guided compaction flow helps you tidy up before the window overflows, and overflow errors now carry a clear name instead of repeating the provider's raw message. Stored thinking levels reflect what the model will actually run at inference time.
- **Web font delivery**: Web fonts are cached immutably and served at the correct weight on first paint — no more flash of unstyled text or re-landing webfonts on every load. The `<html lang>` attribute is resolved before the app paints.
- **QR scanner rebuilt**: The web QR scanner now works reliably on devices without Google Mobile Services and inside China.
- **Chief fixes**: The Chief title stays centered alongside the context meter. Per-turn preambles are excluded from session history. The Chief no longer re-watches on every wake turn.
- **Chat fixes**: Finished-turn replays no longer flash back to life. Streamed prose replays correctly on reconnect.
- **Review safeguards**: Unattended review loops break after five agent-requested rounds. Reviewer quotes are verified against the diff before a revision runs.
- **Team security**: The team member list endpoint now gates on membership.
- **Shell & sync**: Remote-shell exec-channel cold starts are surfaced instead of staying invisible. Sync failures are now countable, and unusable sync destinations are gated.

## 2026-08-02

- **MCP servers**: Teams can add MCP servers — their tools are wired into agent turns automatically. Requires CLI v0.1.45.
- **CLI v0.1.44**: Agents can accept document attachments (not just images). Commit messages no longer carry an extra attribution trailer.
- **CLI v0.1.45**: MCP tool support. Remote shells auto-restart when wedged, send real Enter keystrokes, and ride out reconnects.
- **Turn recovery across refresh**: An in-flight agent turn's prose is restored across refresh and reconnect — no more lost work. PWA cold boots paint from cached snapshots, and turn-opening handoffs are now gapless.
- **Onboarding exit hatch**: The onboarding interview now offers a clear way out, with the cost of skipping it named up front. Tasks are seeded only when the plan is actually accepted.
- **Skill file/folder import**: Restored skill import from files and folders on web and native.
- **Fuzzy ID recovery**: Mistyped IDs (todos, agents, etc.) now recover gracefully instead of answering with a bare 404.
- **UI polish**: Secret form spacing, locked inputs, and team row chrome refined.

Also fixes Windows agents being hijacked by the WSL launcher (all 55 Windows machines affected), and surfaces stale-CLI errors with clear upgrade instructions instead of blaming the repository.
